displayName: loop-sessions: a quarter of the fleet is behind the published build for two days

conditions.displayName: machines behind the published build at or above 7 for 24 h on machines already a day behind

documentation.content:
Seven or more managed laptops (a quarter of the 25-machine baseline) are behind the published build two days after it was published. One machine behind is a laptop that was off; a quarter of the fleet is the upgrade path itself failing: the manifest is unreadable, the published bytes fail their checksum, or the new binary dies on start and the daemon rolls back.

Read one machine's `upgrade` block: `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="fleet version_lag"' --freshness=15m --format='value(jsonPayload.email,jsonPayload.agent_version,jsonPayload.hours_behind)'` names them; /admin/fleet shows the same rows. Then `gsutil ls -L gs://__RELEASE_BUCKET__/latest/` and `curl -sS <endpoint>/dl/latest/latest.json` to check the manifest and the artefacts it names agree (README 7b). If the release is bad, republish the previous build from `builds/<sha>/` as the runbook describes; the fleet follows on its next check.

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-upgrade

Cloud Monitoring caps a condition duration at 24 h 30 min, so the two-day rule is written as `behind` (which the evaluator counts only for machines more than 24 h behind the published build) sustained for a further 24 h.
